Hi Ari — answering your questions inline and attaching the runbook + rate matrix.

1) Retries / timeouts
- Non-idempotent (mutating) requests: default 0 retries client-side; if you implement retry, use server-assigned idempotency keys.
- Idempotent requests: up to 3 retries with exponential backoff (base 200ms, multiply by 2, jitter 0..100ms), cap backoff at 3s.
- Timeouts: TCP connect 2s; request-level timeout 30s for generation calls (adjust if you expect >30s).

Python retries example (exponential backoff + jitter):
import random, time
for attempt in range(4):
  try:
    resp = client.call(...)
    break
  except TransientError:
    wait = min(3, 0.2 * (2 ** attempt)) + random.uniform(0, 0.1)
    time.sleep(wait)

2) Rate limits
- Response headers we surface: X-Rate-Limit-Limit, X-Rate-Limit-Remaining, X-Rate-Limit-Reset, X-Quota-Type (soft/hard).
- We provide soft quota with 429 warnings (Retry-After header) and a hard quota which returns 403 when exceeded. See attached rate_limits_matrix.xlsx for your expected tiers and recommended client behavior.

3) Endpoint migration / rollback
- Recommended: canary traffic (5% -> 25% -> 100%) via our routing layer. This allows instant rollback by routing to previous pool. DNS swap is possible but slower to rollback because of TTLs.
- We’ll include a proxy fallback recipe in migration_runbook.pdf that flips routing on health-check failure.

4) STS / token rotation
- SDK supports short-lived credentials. We built a refresh hook; sample in sdksample.zip demonstrates exchange with your STS endpoint and automatic refresh in the background.

Cutover suggestion: 2027-02-10 09:00 PST start for 5% canary, progress after two successful 30-min gates. I attached the migration_runbook.pdf and rate_limits_matrix.xlsx. Also linking the living runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-datawave-cutover (editable by your team).

Attached: migration_runbook.pdf, rate_limits_matrix.xlsx.
